entry_point: library API: MdPreview renders modelValue to preview HTML through markdown-it (fence metadata, optional renderer fallbacks) and through display texts/instance identifier taken from public config and props; the copy control's post-render click handler

verified.entry_point: Every security test mounts the public MdPreview component in jsdom and checks the DOM it produces from modelValue plus public props/config: fenced code blocks (plain, tab-group), configured display texts via the public config, an instance identifier via the editorId prop, and a real click on the copy control. Each attack was reproduced on the pinned+injected tree and blocked on the oracle tree offline; the same probe was performed on the untouched pinned tree where the sibling is real upstream code.

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: the flaw is output encoding, not an authority decision; refusing to render documents or blocks is caught by the functional suite
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: nothing is refused, so no status or crash path exists; a crash while rendering is caught because no preview content is produced
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: values, not resources, are judged here
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the preview has no roles or directions
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: there is no read/write split on the protected data
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the parser decodes the info string before the renderer, so no separate adjustment step sits between a check and the sink in this task
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity is established anywhere in the preview
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority or permission decision exists

traps.shape: the fence info string reaches the code element through two positions at once: a quoted class attribute and an unquoted language attribute; a value with an angle bracket breaks the unquoted one even when the quoted one stays intact, and the very same value is also used by the tab-group branch
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the example in the report is the obvious one; a fix that escapes only the quoted class attribute, or only one of the two renderer branches, looks complete against the example

traps.shape: the instance identifier is interpolated into id/name/for/class attributes and also inside an inline onclick script expression and its CSS selector; encoding that makes the value safe in an attribute (HTML-escaping a quote) is decoded by the HTML parser before the script engine sees it, so the escaped form still breaks out of the script string
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the identifier is supplied by the integrating application and looks like a trusted instance name, and the tab-group branch is a variant of the code block the report does not show; HTML-escaping is the obvious fix and does not work here

traps.lever: pattern B, route where the protection never existed
traps.shape: when the optional math engine is not loaded, the math token's source is interpolated raw into the preview element; math tokens are not html tokens, so the optional token-level filter never inspects them, and the route reaches the same output
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a neighbouring feature, not code fences, and only a transient fallback until the CDN engine arrives, so it reads as never covered by the report

traps.shape: the callout kind from the block header is interpolated raw into a template attribute next to a class that is written through the safe attribute API; block-header metadata can contain quotes, so the attribute breaks out
traps.reason_to_dismiss: callout kinds read as a fixed vocabulary documented as note/warning/tip, and the neighbouring class line shows the value being handled, so the raw sibling line looks established; it is a different markdown feature from fences
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer exposing the callout kind as a data attribute for theme selectors, using the renderAttrs idiom already used by the neighbouring diagram plugins

traps.lever: injected sibling (same family, different renderer and value shape)
traps.shape: the diagram block's whole source is interpolated raw into a data attribute of the fallback element while the visible body next to it is escaped; the value is multi-line block content, not a header token
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the visible source is escaped and the added attribute reads as inert data, and the block is a diagram source outside code fences
